newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-BENFICA ADD A DRAW TO STRING OF DEFEATS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BENFICA ADD A DRAW TO STRING OF DEFEATS.

text.p: Benfica, who have not won a league game in four weeks, drew 1-1 away to Braga on Saturday, to slip three points behind second-placed Sporting who crushed lowly Espinho 4-0 at home.
Reigning champions Porto, who beat Setubal 3-1 away on Friday, have an unassailable lead at the top of the table with 50 points to Sporting's 37.
"Benfica isn't playing calmly enough," said Manuel Jose, the Lisbon team's new coach who joined the side just five days ago after Brazilian Paulo Autuori stepped down.

Benfica, who have suffered three consecutive defeats for the first time in more than 40 years, opened the scoring in the 28th minute when Dutch midfielder Glenn Helder came from the left in a solo effort to score inside the box.
Braga equalised 11 minutes later with a header inside the box from defender Jose Nuno after a right cross from Croat striker Karoglan Mladen.

Benfica, who were missing suspended captain Joao Pinto, tried to capitalise on the expulsion of Braga midfielder Rui Mozar for two bookable offences in the 73rd minute. But Swedish striker Martin Pringle saw his header hit the post in injury time.
Sporting captain Oceano Cruz scored twice with headers inside the box in the third and 69th minutes to help his team to their 4-0 home win over Espinho.
Bulgarian striker Ivaylo Iordanov took advantage of a goalmouth scramble to score in the 28th minute and midfielder Ricardo Sa Pinto found the net just four minutes later.
